findings.claim: Practice feedback assigns its own mark splits, including ‘1 mark each for any two of...’.
findings.truth: The specification states assessment totals and section totals, not mark allocations for these house-written practice questions. The feedback should state acceptable content without invented splits.
findings.evidence: specification 2.2 Assessments; AQA sample materials distinguish their assessed-question totals from these custom questions.

findings.claim: In the Little Fly coda, all three string-trio instruments play pizzicato.
findings.truth: The coda uses semibreve tremolos in the trio; the vocal and double bass improvise together over a sustained arco chord, and the final double-bass note is pizzicato.
findings.evidence: AQA Teaching guide: Area of study 3 (first exam 2026), pp. 5–6.

findings.claim: In Section B, frame every observation as a fusion of named traditions. That framing lifts an answer into the top band.
findings.truth: Fusion is relevant when a question asks about it, but Section B also assesses focused observations such as dynamics, intervals and tonality. No source supports a universal fusion frame or a guaranteed band outcome.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Music sample set 1, questions 11.1–11.4; AQA Teaching guide, p. 4 and p. 11.

findings.claim: Marks come from three things: name the element, give its exact term, and say where in the track it happens.
findings.truth: Those are useful habits for explanation, but they are not the universal requirements for Section B. Some questions require an identified feature without a location, and credit depends on the question asked.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Music sample set 1, questions 11.1–11.4.

findings.claim: A named instrument is ‘the difference between one mark and two’.
findings.truth: The specification gives no universal per-answer mark allocation for instrument precision. Specific instrument names improve accuracy, but the credit available depends on the question.
findings.evidence: specification 2.2 Assessments; AQA GCSE Music sample set 1.

findings.claim: Practice feedback says ‘Any two of’ and promises ‘Top-band answers’.
findings.truth: The specification does not set a mark split or band outcome for these custom questions. The feedback should give acceptable content without either claim.
findings.evidence: specification 2.2 Assessments; AQA GCSE Music sample set 1.

summary: Both lessons were checked against the supplied specification and AQA’s Area of Study 3 teaching guide. Six findings require targeted corrections or removal of unsupported practice-mark allocations.
